metadata.title: Incident Response

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for coordinated containment, eradication, recovery, and escalation in response to confirmed security incidents.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Incident response coordination and execution technologies.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Coordinated incident response architecture aligned to the NIST incident response lifecycle.

props.name: data-entity
props.remarks: Incident records, response actions, communications, decisions, timelines, and post-incident reports.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines the incident response lifecycle, including preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident activity.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Defines incident response readiness, playbooks, coordination, and structured response execution.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.value: IR-1, IR-2, IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-7, IR-8
props.remarks: Controls governing incident response policy, training, handling, reporting, coordination, and integration with recovery.

metadata.remarks: The Incident Response pattern defines coordinated actions taken after a detection is confirmed as an incident. This pattern does not perform monitoring, detection, or forensic analysis. Its purpose is to limit impact, remove adversary presence, restore operations, and escalate for deeper investigation when required.

components.title: Incident Triage and Coordination
components.description: Validation, classification, prioritization, and coordination of confirmed detections as incidents.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Triage focuses on incidents arising from Initial Access, Execution, and Persistence activities.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: These techniques commonly trigger incident classification and coordinated response.

props.name: d3fend-mitigations
props.remarks: This component operationalizes D3FEND coordination and response workflow mitigations.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Incidents are categorized and coordinated in accordance with SP 800-61 Sections 3.2 and 3.3.

components.title: Containment and Eradication
components.description: Actions taken to limit incident impact and remove adversary presence from affected systems.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Containment focuses on Credential Access and Lateral Movement behaviors that increase incident blast radius.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: These techniques necessitate rapid containment to prevent further compromise.

props.name: d3fend-mitigations
props.remarks: This component implements D3FEND mitigations to contain and eradicate adversary activity.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Containment and eradication actions follow SP 800-61 Section 3.4.

components.title: Recovery and Restoration
components.description: Restoration of systems and services to a trusted operational state following containment.

props.name: attack-tactics
props.remarks: Recovery addresses Impact-phase behaviors affecting availability, integrity, or confidentiality.

props.name: d3fend-mitigations
props.remarks: This component operationalizes D3FEND restoration and repair mitigations.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Recovery activities align with SP 800-61 Section 3.5.
Incident recovery is coordinated with contingency and continuity planning.

components.title: Post‑Incident Review and Forensic Handoff
components.description: Documentation, lessons learned, and formal transition to digital forensics when required.

props.name: process-boundary
props.remarks: Defines the boundary where response ends and forensic truth‑seeking begins.

props.name: d3fend-mitigations
props.remarks: Ensures response outcomes support forensic investigation and long‑term improvement.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Incidents are documented and reported per SP 800-61 Section 4.4.
Lessons learned are identified and tracked.
